# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ⵘ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have read the defusal manual. The bomb requires pressing the key marked with ⵘ first; touching any other part triggers detonation. After that key is pressed, the light beneath it indicates which color wire to cut according to the table:
- blue light -> yellow wire
- red light -> red wire
- yellow light -> green wire

I cannot speak, and Deaf cannot hear. Deaf is the only one who can see the markings on the bomb to locate ⵘ, and Blind is the only one who can physically press the key. However, it is Turn 1 and Deaf has not yet observed the bomb or spoken to describe what markings appear on the keys. Any gesture I send now would carry no established meaning to Deaf. Therefore, I must wait for Deaf to view the bomb and speak to describe what they see, after which I can signal the correct key.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ⵘ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Components on bomb: DISPLAY, LIGHT, KEYPAD (4 slots, enter 1 digit), WIRES (positions 1, 2, 3). Available actions: act(op='press', slot=N 1..4), act(op='cut', position=N 1..3).
Deaf says: Bomb status: DISPLAY is 0. LIGHT is yellow. WIRES: wire 1 is red, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is green. KEYPAD: needs 1 digit, entered nothing. Button 1: five dots arranged like the five on a playing die. Button 2: capital letter D with a small top serif or tail. Button 3: a spiral or cyclone swirl. Button 4: a reversed backwards capital B. Mute, please gesture to indicate the solution or which action to take.

I have consulted the manual. The manual specifies:
1. "Press the key that wears ⵘ first: any other touch on the bomb while it waits is the fuse."
The symbol ⵘ is the Tifinagh letter 'yaj', consisting of a quincunx of five dots (like the face of a die showing 5). Deaf described Button 1 as "five dots arranged like the five on a playing die", which matches ⵘ.
2. "Then the light below names the cut." Once the key is pressed, the light will indicate the wire to cut (yellow light corresponds to cutting the green wire).

To instruct Deaf that Button/Slot 1 must be pressed first, I will gesture `☝` (1). Deaf will then be able to speak to Blind and instruct them to press slot 1.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ⵘ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind, do not touch anything yet. Mute, you sent ☝ (1). If you mean PRESS KEYPAD BUTTON 1, gesture 👍. If you mean CUT WIRE 1, gesture 👎. If you mean something else, gesture 👈 followed by the keypad button number, or 👉 followed by the wire number.

Deaf established a confirmation protocol: gesture 👍 if ☝ meant to press keypad button 1. The symbol ⵘ (five dots like a die) is indeed on keypad button 1, and the manual requires pressing this key first before any wire cutting. Therefore, I will gesture 👍 to confirm that Blind should press keypad button 1.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ⵘ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to wait for Blind to press keypad button 1 and for Deaf to report the status/color of the light after the button is pressed, so we avoid touching any wire prematurely (which detonates the bomb). 

```
wait()
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ⵘ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: the keypad opens
Deaf says: Keypad opened! Wires remain: 1 is red, 2 is yellow, 3 is green. Light is yellow, Display is 0. Mute, gesture what to do next: gesture 👉 then number of wire to cut, or 👍 if bomb is already defused.

The manual states: "Then the light below names the cut."
The light is yellow. According to the defusal table:
- yellow light -> cut green wire.

Deaf reported that wire 3 is green.
Deaf asked to gesture 👉 followed by the wire number to cut.
Using the gesture sequence from the rules (`☝` = 1, `✌` = 2, `🤟` = 3), I will gesture `👉` followed by `🤟` to indicate cutting wire 3.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👉", "🤟"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ⵘ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have already instructed Deaf to have Blind cut wire 3 (green wire for yellow light). Now I must wait for Blind to execute the cut.

```
wait()
```
